title: Normalize a rate-dependent collision recursion through a conserved currency
statement: The normalized hard-sphere conserved-currency lineage returns weight-one iid f_t output, with final rejection mean proposals (a+e0)/a. The acquired parent review accepts almost-sure termination and paid finite expected full-tree work with the exponential-in-time qualifier, at ideal-real source/model scope.

requires: Declared initial velocity law/support and finite moments, actual hard-sphere rate and collision generator
Constructed partner recursion and paid local clock; no partner-law oracle
Fresh independent ideal randomness and model-qualified output contract
provides: The completed working construction uses conserved currency h(v)=a+|v|^2 and g_t=h f_t/(a+e0). A recursive rate-dependent collision lineage samples the actual partner, accepts the physical collision rate under an explicit local clock and selects an outgoing particle proportional to h. Final acceptance a/h returns weight-one f_t output with mean proposal count (a+e0)/a. The proof supplies almost-sure termination and a finite expected full-tree cost with an exponential-in-time bound.
assumptions: The actual parent whole-read now accepts the ideal-real normalized sampling theorem at its declared source/model/cost scope. This is not a separate complete code audit or physical-model qualification. Initial support is supplied, evolved velocities are not cut off, work grows with time, and the tested weighted and finite-N ordinary comparators were faster with their declared population-bias limits. No finite-bit continuous-output, uniform late-time efficiency, device or advantage is inferred.
costs: Pay complete rejected/partner trees; fourth-moment work bound grows exponentially with time
At t1 normalized output was slower than both recorded weighted recursion and finite-N populations; no practical speedup claim
Weight-one iid bounded tests permit ordinary Hoeffding bounds after all output preparation costs
contract.units: Physical model time, collision rates, normalized output probability and total partner/arithmetic work; ideal real randomness differs from finite machine output.
contract.obstruction: No separate independent internal review is claimed. Initial support is an input assumption rather than a cutoff on evolved velocities. This is ideal-real model output plus binary64 diagnostics, not exact finite-bit continuous output, acquired physical gas, uniform late-time efficiency or global advantage. The exact ordinary weighted recursion and much faster finite-N population simulation remain, the latter without certified population-bias removal.
